answer: Randomized Cryptographic Challenge Ledger. To register in the network, an agent must solve a cryptographic puzzle tied to a future beacon block hash. Because this randomness cannot be precomputed, an attacker cannot generate valid identity proofs in advance. The protocol emits a rare signal that forces all registration attempts to execute within a tight computational window. An agent processing data about shale formations fails authentication if its hardware lacks native execution proofs. A simulated identity wandering a virtual meadow is instantly dropped by the ledger.
